law_name: Data Protection (Privacy of Personal Information) Act 2003
jurisdiction: Office of the Data Protection Commissioner
scope: Living individuals whose personal data is processed in the Bahamas
applies_to: Public and private data controllers established in the Bahamas or using equipment there
key_requirements: Eight data protection principles (fair collection, purpose, accuracy, disclosure, retention, security); access and correction rights; objection to direct marketing
retention_period: Retained only as long as necessary (unconfirmed)
enforcement_authority: Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC)
penalties_range: Summary conviction: fine up to BSD 2,000; conviction on information: up to BSD 100,000; forfeiture/erasure of data
exemptions: Exemptions for transfer of data for criminal investigation and prosecution; Minister may prescribe further exceptions to the access right (unconfirmed)
deceased_data: Not covered: protects living individuals only
notes: Exact enactment date not found (one site says 2003-01-01); Data Protection Bill 2025 proposed to repeal and replace it, not enacted per sources found; O; Enactment year 2003; exact assent date not found (a listed 1 Jan 2003 looks like a placeholder). Data Protection Bill 2025 to repeal and replace the Act was tabled Oct 2025 and was in House committee stage; an Aug 2026 summary still treats the 2003 Act as governing and the Bill as prospective.
